questions.question: A proton ($q = 1.6\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$) moves at $v = 3\times10^6\ \mathrm{m/s}$ perpendicular to a magnetic field $B = 0.5\ \mathrm{T}$. Find the Lorentz force on the proton.
An electron moves at $v = 2\times10^7\ \mathrm{m/s}$ at an angle $\theta = 30°$ to a magnetic field $B = 0.1\ \mathrm{T}$. Find the magnitude of the magnetic force.

A particle with charge $q = 2\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ moves with velocity $\vec{v} = 4\hat{x} + 3\hat{y}\ \mathrm{m/s}$ in a magnetic field $\vec{B} = 2\hat{z}\ \mathrm{T}$. Find the force $\vec{F} = q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$.
A current-carrying wire of length $L = 0.3\ \mathrm{m}$ carries $I = 5\ \mathrm{A}$ perpendicular to a magnetic field $B = 0.4\ \mathrm{T}$. Find the force on the wire.
questions.answer:
Force on a current-carrying wire:

$F = BIL\sin\theta = 0.4 \times 5 \times 0.3 \times \sin 90° = 0.6\ \mathrm{N}$

questions.question: A particle with charge $q$ and mass $m$ moves with velocity $v$ parallel to a magnetic field $B$. What is the force on the particle? If the particle then moves perpendicular to $B$, describe its subsequent motion.
questions.answer:
**Parallel to $B$:** $\vec{F} = q\vec{v}\times\vec{B} = 0$ (since $\sin 0° = 0$)

No magnetic force — the particle continues in a straight line.

**Perpendicular to $B$:** $|F| = qvB$ (maximum), always perpendicular to $\vec{v}$.

Since $F \perp v$, no work is done: speed is constant. The force continuously deflects the velocity without changing the speed $\Rightarrow$ **uniform circular motion**.

Radius: $r = \dfrac{mv}{qB}$ (centripetal force = Lorentz force)

Period: $T = \dfrac{2\pi r}{v} = \dfrac{2\pi m}{qB}$ (independent of speed!)

questions.question: An electron moves at $v = 5\times10^6\ \mathrm{m/s}$ at $45°$ to a magnetic field $B = 0.2\ \mathrm{T}$. Describe its path.
questions.answer:
Decompose $\vec{v}$ into components parallel ($v_\|$) and perpendicular ($v_\perp$) to $\vec{B}$:

$v_\| = v\cos 45° = \dfrac{5\times10^6}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 3.54\times10^6\ \mathrm{m/s}$

$v_\perp = v\sin 45° = 3.54\times10^6\ \mathrm{m/s}$

- Parallel component: unaffected by $\vec{B}$ (no force)
- Perpendicular component: undergoes circular motion with $r = m_e v_\perp/(eB)$

$r = \dfrac{9.11\times10^{-31} \times 3.54\times10^6}{1.6\times10^{-19} \times 0.2} = \dfrac{3.225\times10^{-24}}{3.2\times10^{-20}} \approx 1.008\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m} \approx 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$

Combined motion = **helical path** along $\vec{B}$ with radius $\approx 0.1\ \mathrm{mm}$.

questions.question: A wire carries current $I = 10\ \mathrm{A}$ in the $+x$ direction in a field $\vec{B} = 0.3\hat{z}\ \mathrm{T}$. The wire has length $L = 0.5\ \mathrm{m}$. Find the force on the wire.
questions.answer:
$\vec{F} = I\vec{L}\times\vec{B} = I(L\hat{x})\times(B\hat{z})$

$= ILB(\hat{x}\times\hat{z}) = ILB(-\hat{y})$

$|F| = ILB = 10 \times 0.5 \times 0.3 = 1.5\ \mathrm{N}$, in the $-y$ direction.

Using the right-hand rule: fingers point in $+x$ (current), curl toward $+z$ (field), thumb (or palm push) points in $-y$ direction ✓

questions.question: A particle of charge $q = 3\ \mu\mathrm{C}$ moves at $\vec{v} = 2\times10^4\hat{x}\ \mathrm{m/s}$ in combined fields $\vec{E} = 1000\hat{y}\ \mathrm{V/m}$ and $\vec{B} = B\hat{z}$. What value of $B$ makes the net force zero?
questions.answer:
For the particle to travel undeflected (velocity selector):

Electric force (in $+y$): $F_E = qE = 3\times10^{-6} \times 1000 = 3\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{N}$

Magnetic force must be in $-y$ to cancel: $F_B = qvB$ in $-y$ direction.

$F_B = qvB = 3\times10^{-6} \times 2\times10^4 \times B = 0.06B$

Setting $F_E = F_B$:

$3\times10^{-3} = 0.06B$

$B = 0.05\ \mathrm{T}$

This is a **velocity selector**: only particles with $v = E/B = 1000/0.05 = 2\times10^4\ \mathrm{m/s}$ pass through undeflected.

questions.question: Two parallel wires, each carrying current $I = 10\ \mathrm{A}$ in the same direction, are $r = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ apart. Find the force per unit length between them and state whether it is attractive or repulsive. ($\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{T\cdot m/A}$)
questions.answer:
Magnetic field from wire 1 at the location of wire 2:

$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r} = \dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7} \times 10}{2\pi \times 0.1} = \dfrac{4\times10^{-6}}{0.2} = 2\times10^{-5}\ \mathrm{T}$

Force per unit length on wire 2:

$\dfrac{F}{L} = I \cdot B_1 = 10 \times 2\times10^{-5} = 2\times10^{-4}\ \mathrm{N/m}$

Parallel currents in the same direction $\Rightarrow$ **attractive** force.

questions.question: A rectangular loop of width $a = 0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ and height $b = 0.2\ \mathrm{m}$ carries current $I = 5\ \mathrm{A}$ in a uniform field $B = 0.3\ \mathrm{T}$. The field is parallel to the plane of the loop. Find: (a) the forces on each side, (b) the net torque.
questions.answer:
Label sides: top and bottom (width $a$, parallel to $B$): no force ($\vec{L}\parallel\vec{B}$)

Left and right sides (height $b$, perpendicular to $B$):

**(a)** $F_{\text{sides}} = BIb = 0.3 \times 5 \times 0.2 = 0.3\ \mathrm{N}$ (each, opposite directions)

**(b)** Torque: the two forces form a couple separated by $a$:

$\tau = F \times a = 0.3 \times 0.1 = 0.03\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$

Or using $\tau = NIAB\sin\theta$ with $\theta = 90°$ (field in plane of loop):

$\tau = 1 \times 5 \times (0.1 \times 0.2) \times 0.3 \times 1 = 0.03\ \mathrm{N\cdot m}$ ✓
